🔥 gridplayer | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Playing multiple video streams or files concurrently in a synchronized or independently controlled grid layout.
✨ Key Features: • Cross-platform (Linux, Mac, Windows) • Support for any video and audio format (VLC) • Support for (almost) any streaming URLs (Streamlink + yt-dlp) • Hardware & software video decoding • Control video aspect, playback speed, zoom
📖 Summary: GridPlayer is a cross-platform media player built with Python and PyQt5, utilizing the VLC library. It allows users to play multiple videos simultaneously in a configurable grid layout, supporting a wide range of video formats and streaming URLs through integrations with Streamlink and yt-dlp.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 vibe | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Local, private, and efficient transcription of audio and video files with advanced AI processing capabilities.
✨ Key Features: • Offline transcription for enhanced privacy • Supports multiple languages and audio/video file types • Batch processing and real-time preview • Integration with AI models (Whisper, Nemotron, Parakeet) and Ollama for local analysis
📖 Summary: Vibe is a cross-platform desktop application that allows users to transcribe audio and video files locally on their device. It supports a wide range of languages, output formats, and AI models, offering features like batch processing, real-time preview, summarization, and translation.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ Tabminal | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a unified, persistent, and cross-device terminal and development workspace experience, enabling users to code and manage systems from any device.
✨ Key Features: • Persistent terminal sessions • Built-in workspace tabs (files, images, agents, terminals) • Agent Client Protocol (ACP) agent support • Multi-host cluster access
📖 Summary: Tabminal is a cloud-native terminal and workspace application designed for seamless use across desktop, tablet, and phone devices. It integrates persistent server-side terminal sessions, a built-in file and agent workspace, and support for the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) to provide a rich, intelligent, and persistent coding experience.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 robin | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Conducting AI-assisted open-source intelligence investigations on the dark web.
✨ Key Features: • Modular Architecture • Multi-Model LLM Support (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Ollama, etc.) • Streamlit-based Web UI • Conversational Follow-up Questions • One-Click Pivots for suggested queries
📖 Summary: Robin is an AI-powered tool designed for dark web Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) investigations. It utilizes Large Language Models (LLMs) to enhance search queries, filter results from dark web search engines, and generate concise investigation summaries.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 secureml | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enabling developers to build AI applications that handle sensitive data in a privacy-preserving and compliant manner.
✨ Key Features: • Data Anonymization Utilities (K-anonymity, Pseudonymization, Masking) • Privacy-Preserving Training (Differential Privacy, Federated Learning) • Compliance Checkers • Synthetic Data Generation (SDV integration) • Regulation-Specific Presets (GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, LGPD)
📖 Summary: SecureML is a Python library designed to build privacy-preserving AI applications. It offers utilities for data anonymization, differential privacy, federated learning, and synthetic data generation, ensuring compliance with data protection regulations like GDPR.
